solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Used clever remark when turning in defendant

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other, here inside the word for defendant

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a trial

indicators.note: turning means the word for clever remark is read backwards

parts.note: a mot (bon mot) is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A courtroom scene where a witticism is slipped into a defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' is an adjective here, as in 'used to'; 'when turning' reverses the bon mot before 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Used to something means habituated or familiar with it, the adjectival sense here.

clue.text: Doctor in lobby from E London — so awkward

indicators.note: East End (Cockney) speech drops the initial H, so the word for lobby loses its first letter

parts.note: a hall is an entrance lobby

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the word for so

parts.note: thus means so, in that way
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A clumsy medic waiting in an East London lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the H, so HALL becomes 'ALL; 'in' puts MB into THUS to make THUMBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clumsy with their hands is idiomatically said to be all fingers and thumbs.

clue.text: Cook up and about mostly once a month

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word once is used

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October

explanation.surface: Preparing a meal and being out and about roughly once a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of 'once'; C (circa) is the standard short form of about.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook up a story or scheme is to invent or devise it.

clue.text: Film that's European and British in equal parts?

indicators.note: in says the two abbreviations are placed inside the word for equal parts

parts.note: thirds are three equal parts of a whole

explanation.surface: A movie that is an even Anglo-European co-production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in equal parts' reads as 'in shares', but THIRDS is the container: 'in' puts E and B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Birds is Alfred Hitchcock's 1963 thriller about avian attacks on a Californian town.

clue.text: Island's dairyman worked with harvest

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters of the two words being kneaded into a new shape

explanation.surface: A farmhand on an island bringing in the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges DAIRYMAN and HARVEST together; the 's in Island's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha's Vineyard is an island off Cape Cod, Massachusetts, a well-known summer resort.

clue.text: Flower buried in cobweb unadvisedly picked up

indicators.note: picked up, in a down clue, says the letters are read upwards, backwards
buried in says the letters lie concealed within the clue's next two words

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly picks up a buried cobweb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried in' points to EBUNAD in cobwEB UNADvisedly; 'picked up' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is something that flows, a river, and the Danube is a European river.

clue.text: Put on short, retrospective poetry collection

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the letters are read backwards
short says the word for put on loses its final letter

parts.note: added means put on, as in added to the bill

explanation.surface: A truncated, backward-looking anthology of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims ADDED to ADDE; 'retrospective' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a collection of Old Norse poems, preserved in Iceland.

clue.text: Just leave a barrel between tablets

indicators.note: between says the other pieces sit inside the two tablets

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so two tablets give two Es
quit means leave
BL is an abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: Advice to leave a barrel among some pills.
explanation.walkthrough: E is drugs slang for an ecstasy tablet, so 'tablets' gives two of them, and 'between' sets the other pieces inside the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair, and an equitable settlement is a fair one.

clue.text: Drive past, over railroad

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive
ago means in the past
on can mean over, as in on top of

explanation.surface: Directions: drive past and cross the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railroad' is a verb here: to force someone into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad someone is to coerce them, as dragoon also means to force.

clue.text: Artist shouting from the crow's-nest?

definitions.meaning: Sir Edwin ..., Victorian painter of animals
a lookout high on the mast who sights the coast and cries out about it

explanation.surface: A painter who calls out from the top of a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as LAND SEER, one who sees the shore and calls 'Land!'
explanation.definitionFit: Landseer was a famous Victorian painter, known for The Monarch of the Glen.

clue.text: Sweet love having answer for Henry!

indicators.note: having introduces the swap that the word for love undergoes
for says one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: love is nil, nought, in tennis scoring
H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a lover who has the answer for Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having ... for' swaps the H in NOUGHT for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of nuts and honey, a type of sweet.

clue.text: In future stretcher bearer maybe ought initially to provide cover

indicators.note: In at the head means the next piece goes inside the bricklayer's carrier

parts.note: a hod carries bricks, which once laid lengthways in a wall are called stretchers

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of ought

explanation.surface: A medic carrying a stretcher who ought to provide shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A stretcher is a brick laid lengthways, so the hod carries future stretchers; the 'stretcher bearer' is not a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: A hood is a covering for the head, or a folding car roof.

clue.text: Bar or pub containing welcome touch: satellite!

indicators.note: containing says the pub holds the following pieces

parts.note: an inn is a pub
hi is a greeting, a welcome
a touch is a little, a bit
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A pub where a bit of welcome meets a satellite dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts all three middle pieces inside the pub; 'Bar' is a noun meaning a restraint, not a drinking counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is a restraint or obstacle, and an inhibition holds one back.

clue.text: Matched husband with poet, a religious type

parts.note: met means matched, as in met the requirements
an odist is a writer of odes

explanation.surface: A wedding: a husband paired with a pious poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Methodist is a member of the Protestant church founded by John Wesley.

clue.text: "School", Jack means to write, is "tremendous fun"

parts.note: a high is short for a high school
J is the card abbreviation for jack
inks are the means by which one writes

explanation.surface: A schoolboy called Jack declaring that writing is a joy.
explanation.definitionFit: High jinks is boisterous merrymaking, an idiom for lively fun.

clue.text: Coin, old, something you should get from cracker?

parts.words: something you should get from cracker?
parts.note: a Christmas cracker, pulled apart, goes off with a bang

explanation.surface: An antique coin found inside a Christmas cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a British party tube that snaps with a bang when pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: The obang was an old oblong Japanese gold coin.

clue.text: Farmers' movement historically target reforms: about a thousand

indicators.note: reforms means re-forms, so the letters of target take a new shape

parts.note: re means about, concerning
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: An agricultural pressure group setting reform targets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges 'target' to GREATT. The trek was the Boers' 1830s migration; Boer is Dutch for farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Trek was the 1830s migration of Boer farmers from the Cape into the South African interior.

clue.text: Ruin is going to a man with a plan

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
shall expresses the future, is going to

explanation.surface: A schemer who is about to bring ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: George Marshall, US Secretary of State, gave his name to the Marshall Plan for postwar European recovery.

clue.text: Char's function to keep cleaning, ultimately

indicators.note: to keep means the function word holds the next letter within it

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of cleaning

explanation.surface: A char, a British cleaning lady, whose job is to keep cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like the cleaning lady (a charwoman, in British use); here it is the verb to scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: To char something is to burn its surface, and singe is a synonym.

clue.text: Trying Kansas, visiting one city

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: visiting means the state's abbreviation goes into the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: An exhausting trip from Kansas to a single city.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying as an adjective means annoying or wearisome, as is something that irks.

clue.text: Film, very sad, about English revolutionary, that's dragged on

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned right round, so the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film

indicators.note: about means the word for very sad goes around the next letter

parts.note: tragic means very sad

explanation.surface: A review of a tragic film about an English revolutionary that dragged on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes TERAGIC, and 'revolutionary' reverses everything; it is not a political rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokers take a drag, a puff, on a cigarette.

clue.text: Asian holding strike gets more than a piece of one's mind

definitions.text: more than a piece of one's mind

indicators.note: holding means the nationality word contains the next piece

parts.note: a Thai is a person from Thailand, in Asia
to lam is to beat or strike

explanation.surface: An Asian man on strike gives someone more than a piece of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural: more than one piece of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The thalamus is a part of the brain, and more than one are its plural.

clue.text: Mutual dealt exceptionally in the German mark

indicators.note: dealt exceptionally suggests cards handed out in an unusual order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A shared deal involving the German currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mark' suggests the Deutschmark; it is a diacritical mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The umlaut is the two-dot sign over vowels used in German spelling.

clue.text: Winter Olympians somehow impress UK judge

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Athletes at the Winter Games trying to impress a British judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski jumping is a Winter Olympic event, and its competitors are Olympians.

clue.text: The case football administrators brought to court

indicators.note: brought to means the first piece is put next to the second

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body

explanation.surface: The football authorities taking a case to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is the case means it is true, a reality.

clue.text: Girl standing for something upright or grand?

definitions.text: standing for something upright or grand?
definitions.meaning: rhyming slang for piano, of which upright and grand are kinds

explanation.surface: A girl standing up for something honest or grand.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano; upright and grand are types of piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Joanna is a woman's name, and in rhyming slang it means piano.

clue.text: Melody to finish with her Scottish boyfriend?

parts.note: a last one is what comes to finish with
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A girl's final song for her Scottish sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: A last air is a melody to finish with; the question mark flags the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alastair is a Scottish male name, so it could be a lass's boyfriend.

clue.text: One almighty petition letter after all the others sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the pieces are reversed

parts.note: to sue is to petition, especially in court
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A petition to the Almighty, returned to sender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses SUE and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was king of the Greek gods, an all-powerful deity.

clue.text: Confidential if not entirely sober sign one's flipped!

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
a wink is a sign, here a confidential one between people

explanation.surface: A tipsy person confidentially signalling that they have lost their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confidential' colours the sign: a wink is a private signal. 'flipped' suggests losing one's mind; tiddlywinks are counters flipped into a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game of tiddlywinks, small discs are flicked by pressing on their edges.
